issue: Register wobble: 'aku' is the only non-saya first-person pronoun in nodes 33-34 (all sibling anecdote cards use saya; aku is otherwise clustered in the later intimate-register block from id-3180 on). Mixing 'aku' with formal conjunction 'tetapi' in the same clause is also incongruous.

fix.target: Ceritanya saya mau berhemat bulan ini, tetapi ada diskon besar di mana-mana.

issue: Gloss garbled: 'what happened isn't necessarily true' asserts the event occurred and questions its truth, which is backwards — 'belum tentu benar kejadiannya' means it is not certain the thing actually happened at all. Target sentence itself is natural.

fix.english: All that is just what people say; it's not necessarily what really happened.

issue: Gloss tense clash: 'before we knew it, he has now become famous' mixes past 'knew' with present perfect + 'now' — unnatural English that will read as a translation error. Target sentence is a good tahu-tahu use.

fix.english: He used to come to this food stall often; before we knew it, he'd become a famous person.

issue: Sequencing: 'cuma' makes its deck-wide debut here (node-33), 91 cards before its register tip at id-2951 where the hanya/cuma contrast is actually taught. An untipped colloquialism debut violates the heard-vs-modeled discipline the slice otherwise keeps; hanya preserves the sentence and defers cuma to its tipped card.

fix.target: Katanya dia hanya mau melihat-lihat, ujung-ujungnya dia pulang membawa tiga kantong belanja.

issue: 'Sudah diberi jalan lebih dekat' misfires: 'diberi jalan' is the fixed expression 'given way / let through', so the clause reads 'having been yielded to closer' — an English calque of 'given a shorter route'. Indonesian shows someone a route (ditunjukkan jalan), it doesn't give one.

fix.target: Sudah ditunjukkan jalan yang lebih dekat, dia malah memilih jalan memutar.
fix.english: He'd already been shown a shorter route; instead he chose the long way around.

issue: Dangling connective: the card opens with 'Sampai-sampai' but sampai-sampai is a consequence clause that needs an antecedent in the same sentence; as a standalone SRS card it is a fragment ('So much so that...' with no 'so much' stated). Restructure to carry its own cause.

fix.target: Kami tertawa terlalu keras, sampai-sampai tetangga ikut keluar.
fix.english: We laughed too loudly, so much so that the neighbors came out too.

issue: 'salah memakai kacamata orang lain' double-marks the mistake and comes out wrong: salah memakai = put on the WRONG one, so adding 'orang lain' yields 'wrongly wore someone else's glasses'. Natural phrasing is either 'salah memakai kacamata' or 'tidak sengaja memakai kacamata orang lain'.

fix.target: Dia menahan tawa waktu bos tidak sengaja memakai kacamata orang lain.
fix.english: He held back laughter when the boss accidentally put on someone else's glasses.

issue: Heard-particle policy breach: 'sih' is modeled in the learner's own first-person voice, while the sibling particles lho (id-2891) and kok (id-2892) are correctly quarantined inside quoted speech. Policy rule 3: heard language, not modeled language. Quote it and make the tip say recognize-don't-copy, matching the lho card.

fix.target: Teman saya bilang, "Filmnya bagus sih, cuma terlalu panjang."
fix.english: My friend said, "The movie's good, I admit — it's just too long."
fix.grammar: Sih = spoken particle you'll hear everywhere: bagus sih = it's good, I admit. Recognize it — no need to use it.
